attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing Yang-Mills estimate is the same-theory collar trace modulus. It must control singular reflected products as supports collide with the reflection plane, including gauge-invariant nonlocal probes, curvature-composite renormalization, Wilson-loop cusp/perimeter effects, and possible plane-supported contact terms.
steps: Fix a finite family \(F_1,\ldots,F_n\in\mathcal A_+\) and coefficients \(c_1,�\ldots,c_n\). The desired OS assertion is \(Q_S(F,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_jS(\Theta F_i,F_j)\ge0\).
For each \(\delta>0\), replace \(F_i\) by the collar representative \(T_\delta F_i\in\mathcal A_{+,\delta}\). The reflected products now have a gap of size \(2\delta\) across the plane.
Regulated reflection positivity gives \(Q_{a,L}^{\delta}(F,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_jS_{a,L}(\Theta\iota_{a,L}T_\delta F_i,\iota_{a,L}T_\delta F_j)\ge0\).

Assuming RG convergence is valid for this finite reflected collar probe, pass to the cutoff limit and obtain \(Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\ge0\). This uses only closedness of the positive cone in the fixed-collar OS topology.

Let \(\delta\downarrow0\). Since \(\omega_{F,c}(\delta)\to0\), conclude \(Q_S(F,c)\ge0\) for the chosen finite family. As the family was arbitrary, the continuum Schwinger functional is OS-positive on \(\mathcal A_+\).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is valid conditional mathematics, but it does not prove the required trace modulus from Balaban-style multiscale bounds. It also does not prove that the cutoff embeddings, collar maps, and renormalized continuum observables define exactly the same gauge-invariant test algebra. Without those two facts, the argument could establish positivity for a modified or augmented theory rather than for four-dimensional Yang-Mills.

assumptions: For every cutoff \((a,L)\), every finite family \(G_i\in\mathcal A_{+,\delta}\), and every coefficient vector \(c\), \(Q_{a,L}(G,c)\ge0\).

For each fixed \(\delta>0\), finite \(F_i\in\mathcal A_+\), and coefficients \(c_i\), the RG limit of the collar quadratic form exists and equals the continuum collar form: \(Q_{a,L}(T_\delta F,c)\to Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\).

The actual cutoff-removal topology dominates the fixed-collar OS topology \(\tau_{OS}^{\delta}\); this is the place where the word valid is substantive, because convergence must be valid for reflected products, not only for unreflected correlators.

There is a same-theory trace estimate \(|Q_S(F,c)-Q_S(T_\delta F,c)|\le\omega_{F,c}(\delta)\) with \(�\omega_{F,c}(\delta)\to0\), or equivalently the full quadratic form is the trace completion of the collar forms.
The collar maps preserve the gauge-invariant algebra and commute with reflection at the level of reflected products: \(\Theta(T_\delta F)\) is the negative-time collar representative of \(\Theta F\).
definitions: source object: a directed cutoff net \((S_{a,L},\iota_{a,L})\) of reflection-positive, gauge-invariant Schwinger functionals on lattice/regulated observable algebras, with embeddings of the intended continuum test algebra and with fixed-collar RG limits.

target object: a continuum gauge-invariant Schwinger functional \(S\) on the locked positive-time algebra \(\mathcal A_+\) such that every finite OS quadratic form \(Q_S(F,c)\) is nonnegative, hence suitable for OS Hilbert-space reconstruction once the remaining OS axioms are supplied.

controlled interface: the family of finite reflected quadratic probes \(F,c\mapsto \sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S(\Theta F_i,F_j)\), first on collar-separated supports and then through a uniform collar-to-plane trace estimate.

same-theory condition: the limiting observable represented by \(T_\delta F\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\) is the same continuum observable \(F\) obtained from the cutoff embeddings \(\iota_{a,L}F\); no gauge quotient, boundary counterterm, or change of test algebra is allowed to create positivity for a different theory.

\(\mathcal A_{+,\delta}\) denotes the subalgebra generated by gauge-invariant observables whose time support lies in \(t\ge\delta\); its reflected partner lies in \(t\le-\delta\), so reflected products have a positive separation collar.
A trace modulus is a family \(\omega_{F,c}(\delta)\downarrow0\) controlling the finite quadratic form, not merely pointwise convergence of individual Schwinger distributions.

equations.label: collar OS quadratic form
equations.valid_when: The observables \(T_\delta F_i\) lie in \(\mathcal A_{+,\delta}\), so the reflected pairings are separated from the reflection plane and are controlled by fixed-collar RG convergence.

equations.label: fixed-collar closed-cone passage
equations.valid_when: The cutoff embeddings identify the same collar observables and the RG topology is valid for every finite reflected collar quadratic form.

equations.label: trace modulus
equations.valid_when: Boundary contact terms, cusp counterterms, and composite-operator renormalizations are uniformly controlled without changing the target observable.

equations.label: positivity extension
equations.valid_when: The preceding fixed-collar positivity and trace modulus hold for the same finite family \(F,c\).

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A decisive falsifier is a gauge-invariant family, for instance renormalized Wilson loops or curvature composites whose supports collide with the reflection plane, for which fixed-collar positivity is valid but \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\) has no same-theory limit or converges to a value differing from \(Q_S(F,c)\) by a non-neutral boundary counterterm.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is the non-tautological bridge after the closed-cone observation: it converts reflection positivity on separated regulated probes into OS positivity for continuum observables that may approach the reflection plane.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Uniform collar trace completion lemma: Fix a locked gauge-invariant positive-time test algebra \(\mathcal A_+\), reflection \(\Theta\), and collar maps \(T_\delta:\mathcal A_+\to \mathcal A_{+,\delta}\) with supports at Euclidean time at least \(\delta>0\) from the reflection plane. If regulated Schwinger forms are reflection-positive on every collar algebra, the RG continuum passage is valid for every finite reflected collar quadratic form, and the continuum quadratic forms have a same-theory trace modulus as \(\delta\downarrow0\), then the continuum Schwinger functional is OS-positive on the full algebra \(\mathcal A_+\).

assumptions: The positive cone is known to be closed in \(\tau_{OS}^{\delta}\).
The observable embeddings do not vary with the cutoff except by controlled renormalization already included in the definition of \(\mathcal A_+\).
definitions: \(\tau_{RG}\) is the topology supplied by multiscale compactness or cluster bounds for the cutoff-removal sequence.
\(\tau_{OS}^{\delta}\) is the initial topology generated by seminorms/functionals \(S\mapsto Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\) for finite collar-separated families.
Domination means every \(Q^{\delta}(F,c)\) is continuous for \(\tau_{RG}\) after the same-theory observable identification.

equations.label: topology domination
equations.valid_when: The finite reflected collar products are among the observables controlled by the RG estimates.

equations.label: closed cone in dominated topology
equations.latex: S_n\in\mathcal C_{RP},\ S_n\to S\text{ in }\tau_{RG},\ \tau_{RG}\succeq\tau_{OS}^{\delta}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad S\in\mathcal C_{RP}^{\delta}
equations.valid_when: \(\mathcal C_{RP}^{\delta}\) is the cone defined by nonnegativity of all fixed-collar finite OS quadratic forms.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If one can build a sequence of positive cutoff functionals converging in the multiscale topology while a reflected collar quadratic form oscillates or converges to a negative value, then domination fails and the closed-cone bridge is not valid for Yang-Mills.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma separates the formal topological preservation step from the Yang-Mills estimate proving that RG convergence really sees reflected products.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Reflected-probe domination criterion: the formal closed-cone argument proves OS positivity only if the actual RG compactness topology is at least as strong as the initial topology generated by all finite fixed-collar OS quadratic forms on the locked gauge-invariant algebra.

assumptions: The gauge-invariant test algebra includes observables whose supports can approach the reflection plane.
Composite renormalization is local enough to identify possible plane-supported terms.
The continuum Schwinger functional has distributional boundary values for the reflected products under consideration.
definitions: Boundary counterterms are local terms supported on the reflection plane arising in the OPE of \(\Theta T_\delta F_i\) with \(T_\delta F_j\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
Neutrality means such terms do not alter the intended value of \(Q_S(F,c)\) except by an error controlled by \(\omega_{F,c}(\delta)\to0\).
Positive-type boundary terms may preserve nonnegativity but still violate the same-theory condition if they add a new reflection-plane degree of freedom.

equations.label: boundary OPE schematic
equations.valid_when: The reflected product admits an OPE or boundary expansion as the collar width tends to zero.

equations.label: neutrality requirement
equations.valid_when: The full OS form is required for the original Yang-Mills observable algebra rather than for an algebra enlarged by reflection-plane fields.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A nonzero limiting plane term \(B_\alpha\) that is necessary to make the collar limit exist is a falsifier for the same-theory bridge, even if the augmented theory remains reflection-positive.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma names the analytic obstruction hidden inside the trace estimate: positivity may survive after adding boundary data, but the Clay-target theory requires the original gauge-invariant continuum observables.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Boundary counterterm neutrality lemma: a collar trace modulus can hold only if all counterterms generated as reflected supports collide with the plane are either absent, absorbed into the same continuum observable, or contribute a positive-type boundary form that vanishes in the same-theory trace limit.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if a concrete gauge-invariant probe, especially a Wilson-loop or curvature-composite family approaching the reflection plane, yields a non-neutral boundary term or shows that \(\tau_{RG}\) cannot control reflected quadratic forms.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves a uniform estimate \(|Q_S(F,c)-Q_S(T_\delta F,c)|\le\omega_{F,c}(\delta)\to0\) for a generating gauge-invariant algebra, with cutoff embeddings satisfying the same-theory condition.
control_decision.reason: The branch is still producing nontrivial mathematical pressure: the bottleneck is now a precise collar trace modulus rather than vague preservation of positivity. This is a better target for Yang-Mills estimates than repeating the closed-cone lemma.

dependency_updates.description: Split into a formal fixed-collar closed-cone theorem and a nonformal collar trace completion theorem. The formal part is essentially settled; the trace theorem is now the main analytic dependency.

The algebra must be locked before taking collars: \(\mathcal A_{+,\delta}\) should be a subalgebra of the same continuum \(\mathcal A_+\), not a cutoff-dependent replacement. Boundary counterterm neutrality is part of the same-theory condition.
dependency_updates.status: requires explicit algebra and embedding specification

dependency_updates.description: The topology must dominate fixed-collar reflected quadratic probes and also support a boundary trace limit. Ordinary convergence of unreflected Schwinger functions is insufficient.
Need a Yang-Mills-specific analysis of contact, cusp, and composite-renormalization terms when reflected gauge-invariant supports collide with the plane.

falsifiers: falsifier: The multiscale cutoff-removal topology controls separated Euclidean correlators but is too weak to make \(S\mapsto Q_S^{\delta}(F,c)\) continuous for some reflected collar probe; then fixed-collar positivity cannot be passed to the RG limit.

falsifier: A family of Wilson loops approaching the reflection plane requires a cusp or perimeter counterterm with a nonzero finite remnant, so \(Q_S(T_\delta F,c)\) does not converge to the same-theory value \(Q_S(F,c)\).

falsifier: Gauge fixing, BRST variables, or quotienting changes the observable algebra between cutoff and continuum; positivity may be valid on lattice link observables but not on the continuum Schwinger functions claimed as the target.
falsifier: Plane-supported contact terms have indefinite coefficient matrix \(\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_jB_{ij}\), producing a negative limit even though every fixed-collar form is nonnegative.
falsifier: The collar maps \(T_\delta\) fail to commute with the continuum embedding, so the limit \(\delta\downarrow0\) reconstructs an observable different from the original \(F\).
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 173 sharpens the branch from closedness of the reflection-positive cone to a two-stage theorem: fixed-collar positivity is a valid formal consequence of RG convergence, but full OS positivity additionally requires a boundary-value theorem for reflected quadratic forms. The key discovery is that the trace modulus is simultaneously an analytic estimate and a same-theory certificate; if it is replaced by an algebra enlargement or a boundary counterterm, the positivity bridge may be true but for the wrong theory.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Test the trace-modulus obligation on a minimal generating family: curvature-smeared gauge-invariant local composites and small rectangular Wilson loops whose time support is translated from \(t=\delta\) to the plane. Compute or bound the reflected OPE/cusp contributions and check whether their coefficient matrices vanish in the same-theory normalization or create a falsifier.
